title: BxAudio

title: Loudness and mastering
body: Peak level tells you how close a file is to clipping. It does not tell you how loud it sounds. Streaming services, podcasts and broadcasters measure loudness instead, in LUFS (loudness units relative to full scale), and turn loud tracks down to a target. title: Time and pitch
body: Slowing a recording down also lowers its pitch, because that is how playback speed works. Time stretching changes the length and keeps the pitch; pitch shifting changes the pitch and keeps the length. BoxLang Audio does both in plain Java with WSOLA (waveform similarity overlap-add). music = audioOsc( "saw", audioFreq( "A3" ), 4 ); faster = audioStretch( music, 1.25 ); // 25 percent faster: 3.2 s,…

title: Testing audio
body: Sound is numbers, so a test can check it. You do not need to listen to find out that a fade is missing, a file clips, or a clip is the wrong length. These checks run in any test framework; the examples use plain BoxLang assert and read like TestBox. title: Web apps
